mishnayos.summary: The Megillah can be read on five different days of Adar, from the 11th to the 15th. Cities that had a wall in the days of Yehoshua read on the 15th, other towns on the 14th, and villages may read earlier.

chunks.en: The Megillah is read on the eleventh,
chunks.st: The Megilla is read on the eleventh,

words.note: The scroll of Esther, read on Purim.

chunks.en: on the twelfth,
chunks.st: on the twelfth,

chunks.en: on the thirteenth,
chunks.st: on the thirteenth,

chunks.en: on the fourteenth,
chunks.st: on the fourteenth,

chunks.en: or on the fifteenth of Adar,
chunks.st: or on the fifteenth of the month of Adar,

chunks.en: not earlier and not later.
chunks.st: not earlier and not later.
chunks.stMore: The mishna explains the circumstances when the Megilla is read on each of these days.

chunks.en: Big cities that have had a wall around them
chunks.st: Cities [kerakin] that have been surrounded by a wall

chunks.en: since the days of Yehoshua bin Nun
chunks.st: since the days of Joshua, son of Nun,

words.note: Yehoshua led the Jewish people into Eretz Yisrael after Moshe.

chunks.en: read it on the fifteenth.
chunks.st: read the Megilla on the fifteenth of Adar,

chunks.en: Villages and big towns
chunks.st: whereas villages and large towns that have not been walled since the days of Joshua, son of Nun,

chunks.en: read it on the fourteenth.
chunks.st: read it on the fourteenth.

chunks.en: But the villages may read it earlier, on the day when people gather in town.
chunks.explain: That is Monday or Thursday, when beis din sits and the Torah is read.
chunks.st: However, the Sages instituted that the villages may advance their reading to the day of assembly,
chunks.stMore: i.e., Monday or Thursday, when the rabbinical courts are in session and the Torah is read publicly, and the villagers therefore come to the larger towns.

words.note: Monday or Thursday, when village people came into town.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah shows which day each kind of place reads the Megillah, depending on which day of the week the 14th of Adar falls.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. חָל לִהְיוֹת יוֹם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר בַּשֵּׁנִי,
chunks.en: How so? If the fourteenth falls on Monday,
chunks.st: How so? If the fourteenth of Adar occurs on Monday,

chunks.he: כְּפָרִים וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: villages and big towns read it on that day,
chunks.st: the villages and large towns read it on that day,

chunks.en: and walled cities read it the next day.
chunks.st: and the walled cities read it on the next day, the fifteenth.

chunks.en: If it falls on Tuesday or Wednesday,
chunks.st: If the fourteenth occurs on Tuesday or Wednesday,

chunks.en: the villages read early, on the day of gathering,
chunks.st: the villages advance their reading to the day of assembly, i.e., Monday, the twelfth or thirteenth of Adar;

chunks.en: the big towns read it on that day,
chunks.st: the large towns read it on that day, i.e., the fourteenth of Adar,

chunks.en: and the walled cities the next day.
chunks.st: and the walled cities read it on the next day, the fifteenth.

chunks.en: If it falls on Thursday,
chunks.st: If the fourteenth occurs on Thursday,

chunks.he: כְּפָרִים וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: villages and big towns read it on that day,
chunks.st: the villages and large towns read it on that day, the fourteenth,

chunks.en: and the walled cities the next day.
chunks.st: and the walled cities read it on the next day, the fifteenth.

chunks.en: If it falls on Friday, erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the fourteenth occurs on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: the villages read early, on the day of gathering,
chunks.st: the villages advance their reading to the day of assembly, i.e., Thursday, the thirteenth of Adar;

chunks.en: and the big towns and the walled cities
chunks.st: and the large towns and the walled cities

chunks.en: read it on that day.
chunks.explain: The walled cities don't read on Shabbos, so they read on Friday too.
chunks.st: read it on that day, i.e., the fourteenth of Adar.
chunks.stMore: Even the walled cities read the Megilla on the fourteenth rather than on the fifteenth, as they do not read it on Shabbat.

chunks.en: If it falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the fourteenth occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: villages and big towns read early
chunks.st: both the villages and large towns advance

chunks.en: on the day of gathering,
chunks.st: their reading to the day of assembly, i.e., Thursday, the twelfth of Adar;

chunks.en: and the walled cities the next day.
chunks.st: and the walled cities read it on the day after Purim, the fifteenth.

chunks.en: If it falls on Sunday, after Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the fourteenth occurs on Sunday,

chunks.en: the villages read early, on the day of gathering,
chunks.st: the villages advance their reading to the day of assembly, i.e., Thursday, the eleventh of Adar;

chunks.en: the big towns read it on that day,
chunks.st: and the large towns read it on that day, i.e., the fourteenth of Adar;

chunks.en: and the walled cities the next day.
chunks.st: and the walled cities read it on the next day, the fifteenth.

mishnayos.summary: A "big town" is one with ten men who are always free to come to shul. The Megillah may be read early but not late, while some other mitzvos are pushed off instead of being done early.

chunks.en: What is a big town?
chunks.st: What is considered a large city, where the Megilla is read on the fourteenth of Adar?

chunks.en: Any town that has ten men free to be in shul.
chunks.explain: Ten men always free from work, so there is always a minyan.
chunks.st: Any city in which there are ten idlers.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains they are always free to be in shul for davening.

words.note: Men who don't work, so they can always come to shul.

chunks.en: Fewer than that,
chunks.st: However, if there are fewer than that,

chunks.en: it counts as a village.
chunks.st: it is considered a village, even if it has many inhabitants.

chunks.en: About these days they said: read earlier, not later.
chunks.st: It was with regard to these times for reading the Megilla that the Sages said that one advances the reading of the Megilla before the fourteenth of Adar and one does not postpone the reading to after its proper time.

chunks.he: אֲבָל זְמַן עֲצֵי כֹהֲנִים וְתִשְׁעָה בְאָב,
chunks.en: But the day of the Kohanim's wood gift, and Tishah B'Av,
chunks.st: However, with regard to the time when families of priests donate wood for the fire on the altar, which were times those families would treat as Festivals; as well as the fast of the Ninth of Av;

words.note: Families gave wood for the fire on the mizbe'ach on their special day.

chunks.en: the chagigah korban and hakhel,
chunks.explain: Hakhel: everyone gathered to hear the king read from the Torah.
chunks.st: the Festival peace-offering that was brought on the Festivals; and the commandment of assembly [hakhel]
chunks.stMore: of the entire Jewish people in the Temple courtyard on Sukkot in the year following the Sabbatical year to hear the king read the book of Deuteronomy;

words.note: A korban brought on Yom Tov.
The big gathering after the shemittah year.

chunks.en: are pushed later, not earlier.
chunks.explain: If they fall on Shabbos, they are done after Shabbos.
chunks.st: one postpones their observance until after Shabbat and does not advance their observance to before Shabbat.

chunks.en: Even though they said
chunks.st: The mishna continues: Even though the Sages said

chunks.en: the Megillah is read earlier, not later,
chunks.st: that one advances the time for reading the Megilla and one does not postpone the reading,

chunks.en: people may still give eulogies and fast on those days, but gifts for the poor are given then.
chunks.explain: Those early days are not really Purim.
chunks.st: one is permitted to eulogize and fast on these days, as they are not actually Purim; nevertheless, gifts for the poor are distributed on this day.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: When is this? In a place where people come to town on Monday and Thursday.
chunks.st: When is the Megilla read on the day of assembly, before the fourteenth of Adar? In a place where the villagers generally enter town on Monday and Thursday.

chunks.en: But in a place where they don't come in
chunks.st: However, in a place where they do not generally enter town

chunks.en: on Monday or on Thursday,
chunks.st: on Monday and Thursday,

chunks.en: they read it only at its proper time.
chunks.st: one may read the Megilla only in its designated time, the fourteenth of Adar.

mishnayos.summary: If the Megillah was read in the first Adar and then the year was made a leap year, it is read again in the second Adar. The Megillah and gifts to the poor belong to the second Adar.

chunks.en: If they read the Megillah in the first Adar
chunks.st: If the people read the Megilla during the first Adar

chunks.en: and then the year was made a leap year,
chunks.explain: A leap year has two months of Adar.
chunks.st: and subsequently the year was then intercalated by the court and now the following month will be the second Adar,

words.en: and was made a leap year

chunks.en: they read it again in the second Adar.
chunks.st: one reads the Megilla again during the second Adar.

chunks.he: אֵין בֵּין אֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן לַאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי
chunks.en: The only difference between the first Adar and the second Adar
chunks.st: The Sages formulated a principle: The difference between the first Adar and the second Adar
chunks.stMore: with regard to the mitzvot that are performed during those months

chunks.en: is reading the Megillah and gifts to the poor.
chunks.st: is only that the reading of the Megilla and distributing gifts to the poor are performed in the second Adar and not in the first Adar.

mishnayos.summary: The only work difference between Yom Tov and Shabbos is cooking food. Shabbos and Yom Kippur differ only in the punishment for breaking them on purpose.

chunks.en: The only difference between Yom Tov and Shabbos
chunks.st: The first is: The difference between Festivals and Shabbat
chunks.stMore: with regard to the labor prohibited on those days

chunks.en: is making food alone.
chunks.explain: On Yom Tov we may cook food; on Shabbos we may not.
chunks.st: is only in preparing food alone.
chunks.stMore: It is permitted to cook and bake in order to prepare food on Festivals; however, on Shabbat it is prohibited.

chunks.en: The only difference between Shabbos and Yom Kippur
chunks.st: The difference between Shabbat and Yom Kippur with regard to the labor prohibited on those days

chunks.en: is that for this one, breaking it on purpose is punished by a beis din,
chunks.st: is only that in this case, i.e., Shabbat, its intentional desecration is punishable at the hand of Man,
chunks.stMore: as he is stoned by a court based on the testimony of witnesses who forewarned the transgressor;

chunks.en: and for that one, breaking it on purpose is punished with kares.
chunks.explain: Kares is a punishment that comes from Hashem.
chunks.st: and in that case, i.e., Yom Kippur, its intentional desecration is punishable at the hand of God, with karet.

mishnayos.stIntro: The previous mishna concluded with the formula: The difference between…is only, thereby distinguishing between the halakhot in two different cases. The following mishnayot employ the same formula and distinguish between the halakhot in cases unrelated to Purim and the Megilla.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah compares two kinds of vows: one who may get nothing at all from his friend and one who may only not eat his food. It also compares two kinds of promised korbanos.

chunks.en: The only difference between one who vowed to get no benefit from his friend
chunks.st: The difference between one for whom benefit from another is forbidden by vow

chunks.en: and one who vowed not to eat his food
chunks.st: and one for whom benefit from another’s food is forbidden by vow

chunks.en: is stepping on his land
chunks.st: is only with regard to stepping foot on his property,

chunks.he: וְכֵלִים שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין בָּהֶן אֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ.
chunks.en: and borrowing tools that are not used for making food.
chunks.explain: The first may not do these; the second may.
chunks.st: and with regard to borrowing utensils from him that one does not use in the preparation of food,
chunks.stMore: but for other purposes; as those two benefits are prohibited to the former, but permitted to the latter.

chunks.en: The only difference between a "neder" korban and a "nedavah" korban
chunks.explain: For a neder he said "I will bring a korban"; for a nedavah he said "this animal is a korban."
chunks.st: The difference between animals consecrated to the Temple as vow offerings and animals consecrated as gift offerings

chunks.en: is that for a neder, he must replace it if it is lost,
chunks.st: is only that in the case of vow offerings, if they died or were lost before being sacrificed on the altar, one is obligated in the responsibility to replace them,

chunks.en: and for a nedavah, he does not need to replace it.
chunks.st: and in the case of gift offerings, if they died or were lost, one is not obligated in the responsibility to replace them.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches small differences between kinds of tumah: a zav who saw two signs or three, and a metzora who is only waiting or one who is surely a metzora.

chunks.he: אֵין בֵּין זָב הָרוֹאֶה שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת
chunks.en: The only difference between a zav who had two signs

words.note: A person who became tamei from a kind of sickness.

chunks.en: and one who had three is a korban.
chunks.explain: The one with three signs brings a korban when he becomes better.

chunks.en: The only difference between a metzora who is waiting

words.note: Someone with tzaraas, a skin sickness.
The Kohen told him to wait to see if it was real tzaraas.

chunks.en: and a metzora who is surely tamei
is letting his hair grow wild and tearing his clothes.
chunks.explain: Only the sure metzora must do these.

chunks.en: The only difference between one who became pure after waiting
and one who became pure after being surely tamei
is shaving and bringing birds.
chunks.explain: Only the one who was surely a metzora does these.

mishnayos.summary: A sefer of Tanach may be written in any language, but tefillin and mezuzos only in holy Hebrew letters. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says sefarim may also be written only in Greek.

chunks.en: The only difference between sefarim and tefillin and mezuzos
chunks.st: The difference between Torah scrolls, and phylacteries and mezuzot,
chunks.stMore: in terms of the manner in which they are written,

words.note: Scrolls of the Torah and Tanach.

chunks.en: is that sefarim may be written in any language,
chunks.st: is only that Torah scrolls are written in any language,

chunks.he: וּתְפִלִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת אֵינָן נִכְתָּבוֹת אֶלָּא אַשּׁוּרִית.
chunks.en: but tefillin and mezuzos are written only in Ashuris.
chunks.explain: Ashuris is the holy Hebrew writing.
chunks.st: whereas phylacteries and mezuzot are written only in Ashurit,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in Hebrew and using the Hebrew script.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Even for sefarim they only allowed
chunks.st: Even with regard to Torah scrolls,

chunks.en: them to be written in Greek.
chunks.explain: Besides Hebrew, the only other language allowed is Greek.
chunks.st: the Sages permitted them to be written only in Greek.
chunks.stMore: Torah scrolls written in any other language do not have the sanctity of a Torah scroll.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches differences between kinds of Kohen Gadol: one anointed with the holy oil and one who wore the special clothes, and one serving now and one who served before.

chunks.he: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה
chunks.en: The only difference between a Kohen Gadol anointed with the anointing oil
chunks.st: The difference between a High Priest anointed with the oil of anointing,
chunks.stMore: which was the method through which High Priests were consecrated until the oil was sequestered toward the end of the First Temple period,

words.note: The special holy oil made by Moshe.

chunks.en: and a Kohen Gadol who wore the many clothes
chunks.explain: Later, the Kohen Gadol became Kohen Gadol by putting on his special clothes.
chunks.st: and one consecrated by donning multiple garments
chunks.stMore: unique to the High Priest, which was the practice during the Second Temple period,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא פַּר הַבָּא עַל כָּל הַמִּצְוֹת.
chunks.en: is the bull brought for a mistake in any of the mitzvos.
chunks.explain: Only the anointed Kohen Gadol brings this korban.
chunks.st: is only that the latter does not bring the bull that comes for transgression of any of the mitzvot.
chunks.stMore: An anointed High Priest who unwittingly issued an erroneous halakhic ruling and acted upon that ruling, and transgressed a mitzva whose unwitting violation renders one liable to bring a sin-offering, is obligated to bring a sin-offering unique to one in his position.

chunks.he: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְכֹהֵן שֶׁעָבַר
chunks.en: The only difference between a Kohen Gadol who is serving and one who used to serve
chunks.st: The difference between a High Priest currently serving in that capacity and a former
chunks.stMore: High Priest, who temporarily filled that position when the High Priest was unfit for service,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא פַּר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה:
chunks.en: is the bull of Yom Kippur and the tenth of an eifah.
chunks.explain: The tenth of an eifah is a flour korban the Kohen Gadol brought each day.
chunks.st: is only with regard to the bull brought by the High Priest on Yom Kippur, and the tenth of an ephah meal-offering brought daily by the High Priest.
chunks.stMore: Each of these offerings is brought only by the current High Priest, and not by a former High Priest.

mishnayos.summary: In the times when people could bring korbanos on altars outside the Beis HaMikdash, a big public altar and a small private one were almost the same. Only korbanos people chose to give could go on a small altar.

chunks.en: The only difference between a big bamah
chunks.explain: A bamah is an altar outside the Beis HaMikdash, allowed long ago.
chunks.st: The difference between a great, public altar,
chunks.stMore: such as the altars established at Nob and Gibeon, which served as religious centers following the destruction of the Tabernacle in Shiloh,

words.note: An altar, here one for everyone.

chunks.en: and a small bamah is the Pesach korbanos.
chunks.explain: A Pesach korban could not go on a small bamah.
chunks.st: and a small, personal altar on which individuals would sacrifice their offerings, is only with regard to Paschal lambs,
chunks.stMore: which may not be sacrificed on a small altar.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Any korban that is promised or given freely
chunks.st: Any offering that is vowed or contributed voluntarily

chunks.en: is brought on a bamah.
chunks.st: is sacrificed on a small altar,

chunks.he: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא נִדָּר וְלֹא נִדָּב,
chunks.en: And any korban that is not promised and not given freely
chunks.st: and any offering that is neither vowed nor contributed voluntarily, but rather is compulsory, e.g., a sin-offering,

chunks.en: is not brought on a bamah.
chunks.st: is not sacrificed on a small altar.

mishnayos.summary: The Mishkan in Shiloh and the Beis HaMikdash in Yerushalayim were almost the same. In Shiloh, lighter korbanos could be eaten anywhere you could see it from, and after Shiloh people could use a bamah again, but not after Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: The only difference between Shiloh and Yerushalayim
chunks.st: The difference between the Tabernacle in Shilo and the Temple in Jerusalem

words.note: Where the Mishkan stood for many years.

chunks.en: is that in Shiloh they ate
chunks.st: is only that in Shiloh one eats

chunks.en: korbanos of lighter holiness
chunks.st: offerings of lesser sanctity,
chunks.stMore: e.g., individual peace-offerings, thanks-offerings, and the Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: and maaser sheni anywhere you could see Shiloh from,
chunks.st: and also the second tithe, in any place that overlooks
chunks.stMore: Shiloh, as Shiloh was not a walled city and any place within its Shabbat boundary was regarded as part of the city.

words.note: A tenth of the crops, eaten in the holy city.

chunks.en: but in Yerushalayim, only inside the wall.
chunks.st: And in Jerusalem one eats those consecrated items only within the walls.

chunks.en: Here and there, the holiest korbanos
chunks.st: And here, in Shiloh, and there, in Jerusalem, offerings of the most sacred order

chunks.en: are eaten only inside the curtains.
chunks.explain: The Mishkan's courtyard had curtains around it.
chunks.st: are eaten only within the hangings.
chunks.stMore: The Tabernacle courtyard in Shiloh was surrounded by hangings and the Temple courtyard in Jerusalem was surrounded by a wall.

chunks.en: After the holiness of Shiloh, a bamah was allowed again,
chunks.st: There is another difference: With regard to the sanctity of Shiloh, after the Tabernacle was destroyed, there is permission to sacrifice offerings on improvised altars.

chunks.en: but after the holiness of Yerushalayim, it was not allowed.
chunks.explain: Once there was a Beis HaMikdash, a bamah was never allowed again.
chunks.st: But with regard to the sanctity of Jerusalem, after the Temple was destroyed, there is no permission to sacrifice offerings on improvised altars, as the prohibition remains intact.

mishnayos.summary: The Megillah must be read in order and from the scroll, not by heart. It must be read in Hebrew or in a language the listener understands.

chunks.en: If someone reads the Megillah out of order,
chunks.st: With regard to one who reads the Megilla out of order,
chunks.stMore: reading a later section first, and then going back to the earlier section,

chunks.en: he has not done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

words.note: He did not do his mitzvah.

chunks.en: If he read it by heart,
chunks.st: If he read it by heart,

chunks.en: or read it in Targum,
chunks.explain: Targum is the Aramaic translation.
chunks.st: or if he read it in Aramaic translation

chunks.en: or in any other language he doesn't understand,
chunks.st: or in any other language that he does not understand,

chunks.en: he has not done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: But for people who speak another language, we may read it in their language.
chunks.st: However, for those who speak a foreign language, one may read the Megilla in that foreign language.

words.en: for those who speak another language

chunks.en: And one who speaks another language who heard it in Hebrew has done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: And one who speaks a foreign language who heard the Megilla read in Ashurit, i.e., in Hebrew, has fulfilled his obligation.

words.en: and the one who speaks another language

mishnayos.summary: If someone reads the Megillah with breaks or while sleepy, he has done the mitzvah. If he was writing it or checking it, it counts only if he meant to do the mitzvah. A kosher Megillah must be written in Hebrew, on parchment, with ink.

chunks.en: If he read it with breaks,
chunks.st: If one read the Megilla at intervals, pausing and resuming,

chunks.en: or while dozing off, he has done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: or while he is dozing off, he has fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If he was writing it,
chunks.st: If one was writing a Megilla,

chunks.en: or explaining it, or fixing mistakes in it,
chunks.explain: And he read every word while doing it.
chunks.st: or expounding upon it, or correcting it,
chunks.stMore: and he read all its words as he was doing so, the following distinction applies:

chunks.en: if he meant to do the mitzvah,
chunks.st: If he had intent to fulfill his obligation with that reading

chunks.en: he has done it. And if not,
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation, but if not,

chunks.en: he has not done it.
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If it was written with sam,
chunks.st: If one reads from a Megilla that was written not with ink but with sam

chunks.en: or with sikra, or komos, or kankantom,
chunks.explain: These are kinds of colors, not real ink.
chunks.st: or with sikra or with komos or with kankantom,

chunks.en: or on paper or on diftera,
chunks.explain: Diftera is leather that was not fully made into parchment.
chunks.st: or from a Megilla that was written not on parchment but on neyar or on diftera, a kind of unprocessed leather,

words.note: Leather not fully made into parchment.

chunks.en: he has not done the mitzvah,
chunks.st: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: unless it is written in Ashuris,

chunks.en: Any day that has Mussaf
chunks.st: Any day on which there is an additional offering sacrificed in the Temple

chunks.en: and is not Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and that is not a Festival,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the New Moon and the intermediate days of a Festival,

chunks.en: four people read.
chunks.st: four people read from the Torah;

chunks.en: On Yom Tov,
chunks.st: on a Festival,

chunks.en: five. On Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: five people read; on Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: six. On Shabbos,
chunks.st: six people read; and on Shabbat,

chunks.en: seven. We may not have fewer than them,
chunks.st: seven people read. One may not decrease the number of readers,

chunks.en: but we may add to them,
chunks.st: but one may add to them.

chunks.en: and there is a haftarah from the Nevi'im.
chunks.st: And on these days one concludes with a reading from the Prophets.

chunks.en: The one who starts and the one who ends the Torah reading
chunks.st: Both the one who begins the reading and the one who concludes the reading from the Torah

chunks.en: make a bracha before it and after it.
chunks.st: recite a blessing; one recites before the beginning of the reading and one recites after its conclusion, but the middle readers do not recite a blessing.

mishnayos.summary: Some parts of davening and other things need a minyan of ten men. Also, holy land is valued by ten people, nine and a Kohen.

chunks.en: We do not start the Shema brachos for others,
chunks.explain: One says Barchu and the first bracha before Shema for the people.
chunks.st: One does not recite the introductory prayers and blessing [poresin] before Shema;

chunks.en: and nobody goes before the aron to lead davening,
chunks.st: nor does one pass before the ark to repeat the Amida prayer;

chunks.en: and the Kohanim do not lift their hands,
chunks.explain: To say Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: nor do the priests lift their hands to recite the Priestly Benediction;

chunks.en: and we do not read from the Torah,
chunks.st: nor is the Torah read in public;

chunks.en: and there is no haftarah from the Nevi'im,
chunks.st: nor does one conclude with a reading from the Prophets [haftara] in the presence of fewer than ten men.

chunks.en: and we do not do the standing and sitting at a funeral,
chunks.st: And one does not observe the practice of standing up and sitting down for the delivery of eulogies at a funeral service;

chunks.en: and we do not say the mourners' bracha,
chunks.st: nor does one recite the mourners’ blessing or

chunks.en: or comfort the mourners, or say the chassan's brachos,
chunks.explain: The chassan's brachos are the Sheva Brachos at a wedding.
chunks.st: comfort mourners in two lines after the funeral; or recite the bridegrooms’ blessing;

chunks.en: and we do not say "Let us bless our G-d" in bentching
chunks.st: and one does not invite others to recite Grace after Meals, i.e., conduct a zimmun, with the name of God,

chunks.en: with fewer than ten.
chunks.st: with fewer than ten men present.

chunks.en: And for land, nine and a Kohen.
chunks.explain: Ten people, one a Kohen, decide how much holy land is worth.
chunks.st: If one consecrated land and now wishes to redeem it, the land must be assessed by nine men and one priest, for a total of ten.

chunks.en: And the same for a person.
chunks.explain: When someone promised his own value to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: And similarly, assessing the value of a person who has pledged his own value to the Temple must be undertaken by ten people, one of whom must be a priest.

mishnayos.summary: The Torah reader must read at least three pesukim, and gives the translator only one pasuk at a time. In the Navi we may skip around a little, but not in the Torah.

chunks.he: הַקּוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה לֹא יִפְחֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה פְסוּקִים.
chunks.en: One who reads in the Torah may not read fewer than three pesukim.
chunks.st: One who reads from the Torah in the synagogue should not read fewer than three verses.

chunks.he: לֹא יִקְרָא לַמְּתֻרְגְּמָן יוֹתֵר מִפָּסוּק אֶחָד,
chunks.en: He may not read more than one pasuk at a time to the translator,
chunks.explain: The translator said each pasuk in Aramaic for everyone.
chunks.st: And when it is being translated, he should not read to the translator more than one verse at a time,
chunks.stMore: so that the translator will not become confused.

chunks.en: and in the Navi, three.
chunks.st: And with regard to the Prophets, one may read to the translator three verses at a time.
chunks.stMore: With respect to the Torah, an incorrect translation might lead to an error in practice, but this concern does not apply to the Prophets.

chunks.en: If the three were three separate parshiyos,
chunks.st: If the three verses constitute three separate paragraphs,
chunks.stMore: that is to say, if each verse is a paragraph in itself,

chunks.en: he reads them one by one.
chunks.st: one must read them to the translator one by one.

chunks.en: We may skip around in the Navi, but we may not skip in the Torah.
chunks.st: One may skip from one place to another while reading the Prophets, but one may not skip from one place to another while reading the Torah.

chunks.en: And how far may he skip?
chunks.st: How far may he skip?

chunks.en: As far as he can before the translator finishes.
chunks.explain: The people should not have to wait for him.
chunks.st: As far as he can, provided that the translator will not conclude his translation while the reader is still rolling the scroll to the new location. The reader may not cause the congregation to wait for him after the translator has finished, as that would be disrespectful to the congregation.

mishnayos.summary: The one who reads the haftarah gets the honor of saying the Shema brachos, leading davening and duchening if he is a Kohen. If he is a child, his father or rebbi leads instead.

chunks.en: The one who reads the haftarah from the Navi,
chunks.st: The one who concludes with a reading from the Prophets [haftara]

words.en: the one who reads the haftarah

chunks.en: he starts the Shema brachos,
chunks.st: is also the one who is honored to recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema,

chunks.en: and he leads the davening before the aron,
chunks.st: and he passes before the ark to repeat the Amida prayer,

chunks.en: and he lifts his hands for Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: and if he is a priest he lifts his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction.

chunks.en: And if he was a child,
chunks.st: And if the one who reads the haftara is a minor,
chunks.stMore: who may read the haftara but is not qualified to lead the congregation in prayer,

chunks.he: אָבִיו אוֹ רַבּוֹ עוֹבְרִין עַל יָדוֹ:
chunks.en: his father or his rebbi leads the davening in his place.
chunks.st: his father or teacher is honored to pass before the ark in his place.

mishnayos.summary: A child may read the Torah but may not lead the davening. A person in torn clothes may not read the Torah or lead. A blind person may still say the brachos of Shema, but Rabbi Yehudah disagrees about someone blind from birth.

chunks.en: A child may read from the Torah and translate it,
chunks.st: A minor may read the Torah in public and also translate the text for the congregation into Aramaic,

chunks.en: but he may not start the Shema brachos,
chunks.st: but he may not recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema,

chunks.en: and he may not lead the davening before the aron,
chunks.st: and he may not pass before the ark to lead the congregation in prayer,

chunks.en: and he may not lift his hands for Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: and he may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction.

chunks.en: A person in torn clothes may start the Shema brachos and translate,
chunks.explain: His clothes are torn so his arms show.
chunks.st: One whose limbs are exposed [poḥe’aḥ] may recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema and translate the Torah reading into Aramaic,

words.note: A person whose clothes are torn.

chunks.en: but he may not read from the Torah,
chunks.explain: Out of respect for the Torah.
chunks.st: but he may not read from the Torah out of respect for the Torah;

chunks.en: and he may not lead the davening before the aron,
chunks.st: he may not pass before the ark to lead the congregation in prayer;

chunks.en: and he may not lift his hands for Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.explain: Out of respect for the people.
chunks.st: and he may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction out of respect for the congregation.

chunks.en: A blind person may start the Shema brachos and translate.
chunks.st: One who is blind may recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema, and he may also translate the Torah reading into Aramaic.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: anyone who never saw the lights in his life,
chunks.explain: The sun, moon and stars. He was blind from birth.
chunks.st: Anyone who has not seen the luminaries, the sun, moon, and stars, in his life, i.e., he was blind from birth,

chunks.en: may not start the Shema brachos.
chunks.explain: The first bracha before Shema is about the lights.
chunks.st: may not recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema. The first of the blessings before Shema is the blessing over the luminaries, and one who has never seen them cannot recite the blessing at all.

mishnayos.summary: A Kohen with marks on his hands may not duchen, because people will look at his hands. Rabbi Yehudah says the same about a Kohen whose hands are dyed blue or red.

chunks.en: A Kohen who has blemishes on his hands
chunks.st: A priest who has blemishes on his hands

words.note: Marks or problems on the body.

chunks.en: may not lift his hands for Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.explain: People would look at his hands, and we may not look then.
chunks.st: may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction.
chunks.stMore: Because of his blemish, people will look at his hands, and it is prohibited to look at the hands of the priests during the Priestly Benediction.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even one whose hands were
chunks.st: Even one whose hands were

chunks.en: colored with blue or red dye,
chunks.st: colored with satis, a blue dye,

chunks.en: may not lift his hands for Birkas Kohanim,
chunks.st: may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction

chunks.en: because the people will look at him.
chunks.st: because the congregation will look at him.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who insists on wearing special clothes or shoes to lead davening may not lead at all. Tefillin must be square and worn in the right place, the way the Sages taught.

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר אֵינִי עוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּבָה בִצְבוּעִין,
chunks.en: One who says, I won't lead davening in colored clothes,
chunks.st: One who says: I will not pass before the ark to lead the prayer service in colored garments,

chunks.en: may not lead even in white clothes.
chunks.explain: We worry he does not follow the ways of the Sages.
chunks.st: may not pass before the ark to lead the prayer service even in white garments.
chunks.stMore: There is concern that one who insists on wearing clothing of a specific color during his prayers is a heretic and therefore unfit to lead the service.

chunks.en: If he says, I won't lead in sandals,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one says: I will not pass before the ark wearing sandals,

chunks.en: he may not lead even barefoot.
chunks.st: he may not pass before it even barefoot,
chunks.stMore: as he is not acting in accordance with the teachings of the Sages.

chunks.en: One who makes his tefillin round,
chunks.st: One who constructs his phylacteries in a round shape

chunks.en: it is dangerous and it is not a mitzvah.
chunks.explain: Tefillin must be square.
chunks.st: exposes himself to danger during times of persecution, when foreign governments impose a ban on the mitzva of phylacteries, and yet he does not fulfill the mitzva to don phylacteries,
chunks.stMore: as phylacteries must be square.

chunks.en: If he put them on his forehead
chunks.explain: The head tefillin go above where the hair starts.
chunks.st: If one placed the phylacteries worn on the head on his forehead, and not in its proper place above his hairline,

chunks.en: or on his palm,
chunks.explain: The hand tefillin go on the upper arm.
chunks.st: or if he placed the phylacteries worn on the arm on his palm, and not on his bicep,

chunks.en: this is the way of the minim.
chunks.explain: Minim are people who don't believe in the teachings of the Sages.
chunks.st: this is the way of the heretics,
chunks.stMore: i.e., those who reject the tradition of the Sages with regard to the proper placement of the phylacteries.

words.note: People who don't believe in the Sages' teachings.

chunks.en: If he covered them with gold,
chunks.st: If one plated his phylacteries with gold

chunks.en: or put the hand tefillin on his sleeve,
chunks.st: or placed the phylacteries worn on the arm on the outside of his sleeve [unkeli],

chunks.en: this is the way of the outsiders.
chunks.explain: People who don't follow the ways of the Jewish people.
chunks.st: this is the way of the outsiders, i.e., those who do not take part in the traditions of the Jewish people.

mishnayos.summary: Some words in davening sound like wrong beliefs, so we stop the person who says them. We also stop a person who changes the meaning of the Torah when reading or translating it.

chunks.en: One who says, "The good people will bless You,"
chunks.explain: We daven together with everyone, not only the good people.

chunks.en: this is the way of the minim.
Or says, "Your mercy reaches the bird's nest,"
chunks.explain: The mitzvah of sending away the mother bird before taking the eggs.

chunks.en: or "For the good may Your name be mentioned,"
or "We thank, we thank,"
chunks.explain: Saying it twice.

chunks.en: we make him be quiet.
One who changes the words of the parshah of forbidden relationships,
we make him be quiet.
One who says, "And from your children do not give to pass
to Molech,"
chunks.explain: Molech was an avodah zarah.

chunks.en: and translates it in a different, wrong way,

words.note: He changed the meaning of the pasuk.

chunks.en: we make him be quiet with a scolding.

mishnayos.summary: Some stories in Tanach are read in shul but not translated, and some are not read at all. Some parts of the Navi are not used for the haftarah.

chunks.en: The story of Reuven
is read but not translated.
chunks.explain: So people won't think badly of Reuven.

chunks.en: The story of Tamar
is read and translated.
The first part of the story of the Golden Calf
is read and translated.
And the second part,
chunks.explain: When Aharon tells Moshe what happened.

chunks.en: is read but not translated.
Birkas Kohanim,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says Birkas Kohanim is read but not translated.

chunks.en: the story of David
and Amnon,
are not read and not translated.
We do not read the Merkavah for a haftarah,
chunks.explain: The Merkavah is Yechezkel's vision of Hashem's chariot.

chunks.en: but Rabbi Yehudah allows it.
Rabbi Eliezer says,
We do not read for the haftarah
"Make known to Yerushalayim."
chunks.explain: It speaks badly about the Jewish people.
